subject: Banking
title: PayPal Started the Revolution
description: A quick win: understand PayPal Started the Revolution.

hook.text: PayPal launched in 1998 to let people email money. It processed $1.36 trillion in payments in 2023.

buildup.text: PayPal solved online trust. Strangers could transact safely with PayPal in the middle.

discovery.text: PayPal proved that payments could happen outside the banking system.

twist.text: PayPal's 'mafia' — founders who left — started Tesla, YouTube, LinkedIn, Palantir, and Yelp.

climax.text: PayPal proved there was a market between banks and consumers. That gap became the fintech industry.

punchline.text: $1.36 trillion in payments. PayPal proved fintech could rival banks.

quiz.question: How much did PayPal process in payments in 2023?

details.summary: PayPal pioneered online payments in 1998 and proved that a technology company could handle money transfers without being a traditional bank, opening the door for every fintech company that followed.
details.whyItMatters: PayPal demonstrated the market for digital-first financial services and trained a generation to trust non-bank platforms with their money. Its alumni went on to found Tesla, LinkedIn, YouTube, and other transformative companies.
takeaways: PayPal processed over $1.36 trillion in payment volume in 2023
The PayPal Mafia alumni include founders of multiple billion-dollar companies
eBay's acquisition in 2002 gave PayPal the platform to achieve scale

faq.question: How did PayPal disrupt traditional banking?
faq.answer: PayPal made it possible to send money using just an email address, bypassing the slow and expensive bank wire system. It particularly solved the trust problem in online commerce where buyers and sellers did not know each other.

faq.question: Why is PayPal considered the first fintech company?
faq.answer: PayPal was the first technology startup to gain mainstream adoption for financial services outside traditional banks. Its success proved the market and model for the thousands of fintech companies that followed.
